# Project documentation and progress

- User-confirmed documentation convention (2026-11-10): keep all project specifications, technical notes, test records, decisions and post-test assessments as flat Markdown files directly under `project/`, organized by feature group and error ID. Do not retain parallel legacy documents or create documentation subfolders.
- The only aggregate tracking documents are `project/PLAN.md` (features) and `project/TEST.md` (errors/observations). Keep them concise: stable ID, short description, status/priority, last update and link to details. Do not put long specifications, test logs, decision histories or detailed backlogs in these indexes; do not recreate `project/README.md` or a separate global implementation-status document.
- Feature/group detail files use `F-xxx-short-name.md`; error detail files use `E-xxx-short-name.md`, with three-digit stable IDs. Allocate the next unused ID; never renumber/reuse an ID. Preserve existing acceptance IDs (AUTH-01, UPLOAD-01, etc.) as separate test references. Related errors link to their F-ID and affected feature details link back to E-ID records.
- Each F detail must explain business purpose, scope, user journey and acceptance in language a product owner can understand; technical design/contracts, security boundaries and code entry points for developers/AI; test cases, dated actual results and post-test assessment; user choices/decision rationale and unresolved proposals; progress, blockers and next steps. Existing English source requirements may be preserved; use clear Vietnamese explanations for the product owner.
- Each E detail must record its linked features, impact, environment/date, reproduction steps and expected/actual behavior, evidence, confirmed or unknown cause, fix approach, regression/retest results and user decisions. Mark unconfirmed observations explicitly; do not label missing features, pending tests or design limitations as confirmed bugs. Never close an error without recorded verification or an explicit user-approved disposition.
- Before implementation, review `project/PLAN.md`, `project/TEST.md` and the relevant F/E detail documents. Shared scope/decisions/delivery history live in F-000, architecture/domain models in F-013, API/backend/infrastructure in F-014 and shared quality guidance in F-015.
- After meaningful implementation, fixes, refactoring or validation, update the affected F/E detail and corresponding PLAN/TEST row in the same change. Put feature-specific evidence with its feature; retain project-wide evidence and governance in F-000. Avoid duplicate authoritative histories. Keep updates concise; avoid unrelated documentation churn for trivial edits.
- Record the validation date and checks actually performed, including relevant test results and known limitations. Clearly distinguish verified results from pending checks; never claim tests, CI, API parity, or production readiness without evidence.
- Preserve existing requirements, acceptance criteria, user choices, unresolved decisions and dated evidence when consolidating documents. Distinguish an explicit user choice from a proposed default, and historical results from newly executed checks. Update incoming links and check local targets/anchors when moving or merging documents.
- Preserve unresolved decisions and outstanding work. Distinguish mock-only functionality from implemented Go APIs and real integrations.
- Before the final response, ensure the documentation matches the delivered changes and summarize any checks that could not be run.
